q: A territory is proposed to be ceded to another country, and it is argued that the Preamble bars the transfer. Which statement reflects the position?
options: Cession requires a constitutional amendment; the Preamble was then held not to be part
Cession requires only an executive agreement; the Preamble was held to be part
Cession is impermissible in any circumstances by virtue of the Preamble
Cession requires a constitutional amendment; the Preamble was then held to be part
expl: The 1960 reference held cession needs an amendment and the Preamble was not then part.
why: Two options give the correct result on cession and differ only on the Preamble holding, so both limbs must be known.
trapnote: This case decided two things. Know both, because options will pair a right limb with a wrong one.

q: An amendment substantially curtails the equality guarantee to advance a welfare objective. Which statement is correct?
options: It is void, fundamental rights being beyond the amending power altogether
It is valid, an amendment not being law for the purpose of the bar
It is void unless ratified by not less than half the State legislatures
It is valid unless it damages the basic structure of the Constitution
expl: Amendments escape the bar but remain subject to the basic structure limit.
why: The third option states a true proposition and draws the wrong conclusion from it, which is the strongest distractor here.
trapnote: A true premise can support a wrong conclusion. The bar is escaped; the basic structure limit is not.

q: Consider: 1-The 1967 decision held fundamental rights beyond the amending power. 2-The 1971 amendment reversed that position. 3-The 1973 decision restored the 1967 position in full. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The 1973 decision did not restore the earlier position; it substituted the basic structure limit.
why: The third statement is a plausible simplification of a complex sequence and is the planted defect.
trapnote: The 1973 decision overruled the 1967 one while imposing a different limit. It did not restore it.

q: A student is refused admission by a private unaided institution on grounds unconnected with any statute. Which statement is correct?
options: A fundamental rights petition lies because education is a public function
No fundamental rights petition lies against it unless it satisfies the State test
No remedy is available at all against a private unaided institution
A fundamental rights petition lies because the institution is recognised by a board
expl: Absent the State test, the fundamental rights route does not lie, though other remedies may.
why: The third option overstates the conclusion into a denial of all remedy, which is a distinct and wrong proposition.
trapnote: Closing one route does not close every route. Distinguish the remedy from the right.

q: An executive instruction not traceable to any statute restricts a fundamental right. Which statement is correct?
options: It is not 'law' capable of imposing a restriction, and the restriction fails
It is 'law' for this purpose, executive instructions having statutory force
It is 'law' only if issued by the State government rather than a district officer
It is not 'law', but the restriction stands if the purpose is a listed ground
expl: A restriction must be imposed by law; an unsupported executive instruction cannot do it.
why: The fourth option accepts the premise and then ignores it, which is the subtler of the two wrong routes.
trapnote: A listed purpose cannot cure the absence of a law. Both elements are required.

q: Consider the 2019 citizenship amendment: 1-It names three countries. 2-It names six communities. 3-It applies to persons who entered India after 31 December 2014. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The cut-off operates for those who entered on or before that date, not after it.
why: The third statement inverts the direction of the cut-off, which is the single most frequently misstated feature.
trapnote: Cut-off dates have a direction. Check whether the provision looks backwards or forwards from the date.

q: A State legislature enacts a law conferring citizenship on a class of residents. Which statement is correct?
options: The law is valid if the President accords his assent to it
The law is valid for State purposes though not for Union purposes
The law is void, citizenship falling within Parliament's exclusive competence
The law is void unless it is placed in the Ninth Schedule for protection
expl: Citizenship is exclusively for Parliament; no State legislature can legislate on it.
why: The third option invents a split between State and Union citizenship, contradicting single citizenship.
trapnote: Single citizenship means there is no State-level citizenship to legislate for.

q: Consider: 1-The bar on laws abridging fundamental rights extends to ordinances. 2-It extends to rules and regulations. 3-It extends to constitutional amendments. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Ordinances, rules and regulations are included; amendments were expressly excluded in 1971.
why: The definition is wide and inclusive, which is precisely why the single express exclusion is the item tested.
trapnote: The definition of law is deliberately wide. Learn the one express exclusion rather than the inclusions.

q: An electoral roll entry is relied on as conclusive proof of citizenship in a verification exercise. Which statement is correct?
options: The entry is evidence but not conclusive; status rests on the Constitution and the statute
The entry is conclusive, inclusion following a statutory verification process
The entry is irrelevant, citizenship being determinable only by a civil court
The entry is conclusive unless the person is shown to hold a foreign passport
expl: A roll entry is indicative; conferral and determination of status follow a different process.
why: The fourth option concedes the general proposition and creates a single exception, which is a common way of dressing an error.
trapnote: Evidence of a fact is not the same as title to a status. Keep the two distinct.

q: A person claims citizenship at commencement on the footing of five years' ordinary residence but has no Indian domicile. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim succeeds: five years' residence is by itself sufficient for the purpose
The claim fails: the required period of ordinary residence is ten years
The claim succeeds: domicile is presumed from long ordinary residence
The claim fails: domicile at commencement is a separate and necessary condition
expl: Domicile at commencement is required in addition to one of the alternative conditions.
why: The fourth option presumes one element from another, which is exactly how such conditions are collapsed in practice.
trapnote: Where a provision has a condition plus alternatives, satisfying an alternative alone is not enough.
